headline: High-risk CVE-2026-96361 batch affects 16 Drupal projects, CVSS 9.8
summary: A CERT-BUND advisory details 36 vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-96361, across 16 Drupal contributed projects, with a CVSS v3.1 base score of 9.8.
details: CVE-2026-96361 is part of a high-risk CERT-BUND advisory (WID-SEC-2026-3554) published on September 23, 2026. This advisory covers 36 identifiers, from CVE-2026-96355 to CVE-2026-96398, affecting 16 contributed Drupal projects.

The vulnerabilities allow for remote exploitation, with outcomes including arbitrary code execution, privilege escalation, security bypass, data manipulation/disclosure, and cross-site scripting. Patches are confirmed to exist for these issues.

The batch has a CVSS v3.1 base score of 9.8 and a temporal score of 8.5, indicating severe affected code paths. This severity rating describes the potential damage, not a confirmed exploitation campaign, which has not been reported.
Key affected projects include Webform, Cloud, Commerce Decoupled Checkout, and Tawk.to Live chat application, among others. In total, 19 fixed releases were issued to cover the 16 affected projects.

Drupal operators should treat contributed modules as a separate maintenance track from core releases. It's crucial to identify which projects in their estate still receive security releases and apply the necessary fixed versions.
Modules that no longer receive fixes should be removed to mitigate risk. For projects with multiple fixed releases, tracking the specific branch in use will streamline future advisory resolutions.
caption:
A batch of 36 high-risk CVEs, including CVE-2026-96361, impacts 16 Drupal contributed projects. These vulnerabilities carry a CVSS v3.1 base score of 9.8.

CVE-2026-96361 is part of a high-risk CERT-BUND advisory (WID-SEC-2026-3554) published on September 23, 2026. This advisory covers 36 identifiers, from CVE-2026-96355 to CVE-2026-96398, affecting 16 contributed Drupal projects.

The vulnerabilities allow for remote exploitation, with outcomes including arbitrary code execution, privilege escalation, security bypass, data manipulation/disclosure, and cross-site scripting. Patches are confirmed to exist for these issues.

The batch has a CVSS v3.1 base score of 9.8 and a temporal score of 8.5, indicating severe affected code paths. This severity rating describes the potential damage, not a confirmed exploitation campaign, which has not been reported.

Key affected projects include Webform, Cloud, Commerce Decoupled Checkout, and Tawk.to Live chat application, among others. In total, 19 fixed releases were issued to cover the 16 affected projects.

Drupal operators should treat contributed modules as a separate maintenance track from core releases. It's crucial to identify which projects in their estate still receive security releases and apply the necessary fixed versions.

Modules that no longer receive fixes should be removed to mitigate risk. For projects with multiple fixed releases, tracking the specific branch in use will streamline future advisory resolutions.
